test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 5 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The kidney of a healthy adult produces 180 L of filtrate daily, but a person throws out only 1 L or 1.5 L of urine. The amount of filtrate reabsorbed depends on which factor/ factors?

options.text: Amount of dissolved waste to be excreted
Amount of excess water and amount of dissolved waste to be excreted

solution:
The correct answer is __**Amount of excess water and amount of dissolved waste to be excreted.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** amount of filtrate reabsorbed** depends on the amount of **excess water **and the amount of **dissolved waste** to be excreted.
 
• This means that if there is **more excess** water in the body, the kidneys will **reabsorb less filtrate** and **excrete more urine.**
 
• Similarly, if there is **more dissolved waste **in the body, the kidneys will reabsorb** less filtrate** and** excrete more urine.**
 
• The reabsorption of filtrate is controlled by the hormones** aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone** (ADH).
 
• These hormones regulate the **amount of water and sodium** that is reabsorbed by the kidneys, which in turn affects the amount of filtrate that is excreted as urine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The amount of filtrate reabsorbed can also be affected by certain medications, such as** diuretics,** which increase urine production by preventing the reabsorption of water and sodium in the kidneys.
 
• Other factors that can affect the amount of filtrate reabsorbed include** blood pressure, blood pH,** and the **concentration of electrolytes **in the blood.
 
• The main keyword in the question is "filtrate," which refers to the fluid that is** filtered from the blood **by the kidneys.
 
• This fluid contains** water, waste products, and other substances **that need to be either reabsorbed or excreted as urine.
